translations.text: Simeon Peter, servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have been allotted a faith of equal honour with ours through the righteousness of our God and Saviour Jesus Christ.
Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ!
He has granted us all the power of his own divinity for life and for godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us to his own glory and virtue.
Through these he has granted us very great and precious promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature and escape the corruption of the lust of this world.
And you also, applying this same eagerness in every way, add virtue to your faith, and knowledge to virtue,
and to knowledge self-restraint (literally "fasting"), to self-restraint patience, to patience godliness,
and to godliness brotherly love, and to brotherly love love.
For when these things are with you and abound in you, you will be found neither idle nor fruitless in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But whoever does not have these things is blind and cannot see, for he has forgotten the cleansing of his former sins.
Therefore, brothers, be all the more eager to make your calling and election firm through good works; for if you do this, you will never stumble at all.
Rather, in this way the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ will be richly provided for you.
For this reason I will not be negligent to remind you of these things always, even though you know them and are firmly established in the truth that has come to you.
I consider it right, as long as I am in this dwelling, to stir you up by reminding you.
I know that the leaving of this dwelling of mine will come soon, as our Lord Jesus Christ made known to me.
And I will make every effort that each of you may be able to remember these things after my departure.
For we did not follow clever tales when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received honour and glory from God the Father, when a voice came to him from the magnificent glory: "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."
And we ourselves heard this voice come from heaven upon him, when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more certain. You will do well to pay attention to it as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
Know this first of all: no prophecy of scripture is a matter of one's own interpretation.
For prophecy never came by the will of men. Rather, the holy men of God spoke as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

There were false prophets among the people, just as there will also be false teachers among you. They will bring in destructive heresy and deny the Lord who set them free, bringing swift destruction on themselves.
And many will follow their impurity, and because of them the way of truth will be blasphemed.
And with covetousness and false words they will make merchandise of you. Their judgment from of old does not rest, and their destruction does not slumber.
For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but confined them in Tartarus with chains of darkness and handed them over to be kept for torment and judgment;
and did not spare the first world either, but preserved Noah, the eighth, a preacher of righteousness, and brought the flood upon the world of the ungodly;
and burned and overthrew and condemned the cities of the Sodomites and the Gomorrahites, and set them as an example for those who would afterward be ungodly;
and rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the lawless who walked in filthiness.
For by what he saw and heard, while that righteous man dwelt among them, his righteous soul was tormented day after day by their lawless deeds.
The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, but the false ones they have kept [?] in torment for the day of judgment.
And especially those who follow in filthiness after the lust of the flesh and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they do not tremble before the glorious ones, but blaspheme them.
Whereas angels, who are greater in might and power, do not bring a blasphemous judgment against them from the Lord.
But these, like irrational beasts of the pasture, born by nature to be caught and destroyed, blaspheme what they do not understand, and they will perish in their own corruption,
and they will receive the wages of falsehood. They have counted [?] lust like a day of pleasure. Defiled and filthy, they revel in their deceptions and feast together with you.
They have eyes full of adultery and of unceasing sin, and they lead unstable souls astray. They have hearts trained in covetousness; they are children of the curse.
They have abandoned the straight way, gone astray, and followed the way of Balaam of Bosor, who loved the wages of falsehood.
As a rebuker of his own lawlessness he had a dumb ass speaking with a human voice, which checked the prophet's folly.
These are waterless springs, clouds driven about by a storm, for whom the eternal gloom of darkness is reserved.
For with exceedingly vain thoughts they draw into the lust of the flesh and filthiness those who have truly escaped, and those who live in error.
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whatever someone is overcome, to that he is enslaved.

For those who escaped the defilements of this world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, if they are again entangled in them and overcome, their last state has become worse for them than the first.
It would have been better for them never to have known the way of truth than, having known it, to turn back from the holy commandment that was given to them.
What the true proverb says has happened to them: the dog has returned to its own vomit, and the sow that was washed to wallowing in the mire.
Behold, beloved, I am writing this second epistle to you, by which I stir up your mind with a diligent reminder,
to remember the words spoken beforehand by the holy prophets, and the commandments of the Lord and Savior given through your apostles.
Know this first of all: in the last days scoffers will come, living by their own desires,
and they will say, "Where is the promise of his coming? Ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything has gone on just as it has from the beginning of creation."
They deliberately forget that the heavens existed long ago, and that the earth was formed out of water and by means of water, by the word of God.
By these the world of that time was flooded with water and perished.
But the present heavens and earth are stored up by that same word, kept for fire until the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.
But do not forget this one thing, beloved: with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord is not slow to keep his promise, as some people think of slowness. Rather, he is patient with you, because he does not want anyone to perish, but wants everyone to come to repentance.
But the day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night. On that day the heavens will pass away violently, the elements will burn and melt, and the earth and the works in it will be burned up.
Since all these things are going to melt away like this, what kind of people ought you to be, in holy conduct and good service, as you wait
and hurry toward the coming of the day of God? On that day the burning heavens will be dissolved, and the elements will burn and melt.
But we are waiting for new heavens and a new earth, as he promised, where righteousness dwells.
So, beloved, while you wait for this, work hard to be found by him undefiled and blameless, at peace.
And think of our Lord's patience as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you, using the wisdom he was given.
He speaks about this in all his letters. Some things in them are hard to understand, and ignorant and unstable people twist them, as they do the other scriptures, to their own destruction.
So, beloved, since you know this in advance, be on your guard. Do not let yourselves be carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your own firm footing.
Instead, grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be glory now and to the days of eternity. Amen.
